title: A Decade in a Day: Synthesizing Agent-Native Interfaces from Human-Oriented Software Evolution
abstract: arXiv:2610.15765v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Large language model agents are emerging as an important new class of users of desktop applications. However, existing desktop interfaces were designed for human end users or application developers, leaving agents to interpret visual controls or discover and compose low-level software operations. This mismatch can hinder even capable agents, yet it remains unclear what interface properties make desktop software easier for agents to use. To study this question, we treat software evolution as a natural source of interface variation and introduce DeskIF-Bench, a benchmark of 255 artifact-verified tasks across six desktop applications. By holding the task, agent, and verifier fixed while varying the software release, we measure how interface changes affect agent performance. translated_title: 一日十年：从面向人类的软件演进中合成智能体原生界面
translated_abstract: 大语言模型智能体正成为桌面应用的一类重要新用户。然而，现有桌面界面是为人类最终用户或应用开发者设计的，这使得智能体只能去解读可视化控件，或自行发现并组合底层的软件操作。这种不匹配甚至会阻碍能力强大的智能体，但目前仍不清楚哪些界面特性能让桌面软件更便于智能体使用。为了研究这一问题，我们将软件演进视为界面变化的一种天然来源，并提出了 DeskIF-Bench——一个包含 255 个经制品验证的任务、覆盖六款桌面应用的基准测试。通过在保持任务、智能体和验证器不变的同时变换软件版本，我们衡量了界面变化对智能体性能的影响。在两个模型与六款应用的实验中，最新版本软件的表现始终优于最旧版本。轨迹分析识别出三种相关的界面特性：……
tldr: 该论文提出 DeskIF-Bench 基准，通过固定任务与智能体、变换软件版本的方式量化界面演进对大语言模型智能体性能的影响，发现最新版桌面软件始终更有利于智能体执行任务，并通过轨迹分析识别出影响智能体易用性的界面特性。
en_tdlr: The paper introduces DeskIF-Bench, a benchmark showing that newer releases of desktop software consistently enable better LLM agent performance, and uses trajectory analysis to identify interface properties that make desktop software more agent-friendly.
